tier1.text: The trapezoid is a small carpal bone that helps form the wrist and the base of the hand. Carpal bones give stability and support while allowing some limited motion. The trapezoid lies between the trapezium and the capitate, which are also carpal bones. The trapezoid also forms a joint with the palm bone that connects to the index finger.

quotes.quote: The only short bones in the human skeleton are in the carpals of the wrists and the tarsals of the ankles. Short bones provide stability and support as well as some limited motion.

quotes.quote: The distal row of carpal bones contains (from medial to lateral) the hamate, capitate, trapezoid, and trapezium bones
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The second and the longest of five miniature long bones located in the palm of the hand, which articulates proximally with the trapezoid, trapezium, and capitate at the carpometacarpal joint and distally with the index finger phalanx at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
